Abnormalities of the heartbeat include conditions such as tachycardia (an abnormally fast heart rate), bradycardia (an abnormally slow heart rate), palpitations (a sensation of irregular or forceful heartbeats), and other unspecified irregularities in heart rhythm. 2. Cardiac murmurs and other abnormal heart sounds can be classified as benign or innocent murmurs, unspecified murmurs, or other abnormal cardiac sounds, including bruits (abnormal vascular sounds). 3. Gangrene, a condition involving tissue death due to lack of blood supply, is categorized separately when not classified elsewhere. 4. 5. Hemorrhages from the respiratory passages include epistaxis (nosebleeds), throat hemorrhages, hemoptysis (coughing up blood), bleeding from other respiratory sites, and unspecified respiratory bleeding. 6. Breathing abnormalities encompass dyspnea (difficulty breathing), orthopnea (difficulty breathing when lying flat), stridor (a high-pitched wheezing sound), wheezing, periodic breathing patterns such as Cheyne-Stokes respiration, hyperventilation, mouth breathing, snoring, hiccups, sneezing, choking sensations, and other unspecified breathing irregularities. 7. Pain in the throat and chest includes localized throat pain, chest pain associated with breathing, precordial pain (pain in the chest area over the heart), other types of chest pain, and unspecified chest pain. 8. Other symptoms involving the circulatory and respiratory systems include asphyxia (oxygen deprivation), pleurisy (inflammation of the pleura causing chest pain), respiratory arrest, abnormal sputum production, rales (abnormal lung sounds), and arterial bruits. 9. Abdominal and pelvic pain includes acute abdomen (severe abdominal pain requiring urgent evaluation), pain localized to the upper abdomen, pelvic and perineal pain, pain in other parts of the lower abdomen, and other or unspecified abdominal pain, including abdominal tenderness and colic. 10. Nausea and vomiting are categorized separately, as is heartburn (a burning sensation in the chest due to acid reflux). 11. Dysphagia refers to difficulty swallowing, while flatulence and related conditions include abdominal distension, bloating, eructation (belching), gas pain, and tympanites (excessive gas in the abdomen or intestines). 12. Fecal incontinence, also known as encopresis, involves the inability to control bowel movements. 13. Hepatomegaly (enlarged liver), splenomegaly (enlarged spleen), and hepatosplenomegaly (enlargement of both the liver and spleen) are classified when not attributed to other conditions. 14. Jaundice of unspecified origin and ascites (fluid accumulation in the abdominal cavity) are categorized separately. 15. Other digestive and abdominal symptoms include intra-abdominal or pelvic swelling, abnormal bowel sounds, visible peristalsis, abdominal rigidity, changes in bowel habits, abnormal fecal characteristics, halitosis (bad breath), and other specified symptoms. 16. Disturbances of skin sensation include anesthesia (loss of sensation), hypoesthesia (reduced sensation), paresthesia (tingling or prickling sensations), hyperesthesia (increased sensitivity), and other unspecified sensory disturbances. 17. Skin changes include cyanosis (bluish discoloration due to lack of oxygen), pallor (paleness), flushing, spontaneous ecchymoses (bruising), petechiae (small red or purple spots), changes in skin texture such as desquamation (peeling) and induration (hardening), and other unspecified changes. 18. Abnormal involuntary movements include abnormal head movements, tremors, cramps and spasms, fasciculations (muscle twitches), and other unspecified involuntary movements. 19. Gait and mobility abnormalities include ataxic gait (uncoordinated walking), paralytic gait, difficulty walking, and other unspecified mobility issues. 20. Lack of coordination includes unspecified ataxia and other coordination deficits. 21. Nervous and musculoskeletal symptoms include tetany (muscle spasms due to low calcium), meningismus (meningeal irritation), abnormal reflexes such as hyperreflexia, abnormal posture, clicking hip, and other unspecified symptoms. 22. Urinary symptoms include dysuria (painful urination), vesical tenesmus (bladder discomfort), unspecified painful urination, hematuria (blood in urine), urinary incontinence, urine retention, anuria (absence of urine), oliguria (reduced urine output), polyuria (excessive urination), nocturia (frequent nighttime urination), urethral discharge, and other urinary difficulties. 23. Cognitive and behavioral symptoms include somnolence (drowsiness), stupor, coma, disorientation, anterograde and retrograde amnesia, dizziness, vertigo, anosmia (loss of smell), parosmia (distorted smell), parageusia (distorted taste), hallucinations (auditory, visual, or other), nervousness, restlessness, unhappiness, demoralization, irritability, hostility, physical violence, emotional shock, suicidal ideation, poor hygiene, bizarre appearance, strange behavior, overactivity, slowness, suspiciousness, undue concern, verbosity, and other behavioral abnormalities. 24. Speech and voice disturbances include dysphasia (difficulty speaking), aphasia (loss of speech), dysarthria (difficulty articulating words), anarthria (inability to articulate words), dyslexia, alexia, agnosia, apraxia, acalculia (difficulty with calculations), agraphia (difficulty writing), dysphonia (voice disorders), aphonia (loss of voice), and nasal resonance abnormalities. 25. General symptoms include fever, headache, acute and chronic pain, malaise, fatigue, senility, syncope (fainting), convulsions, shock, hemorrhage, lymphadenopathy (enlarged lymph nodes), edema, hyperhidrosis (excessive sweating), delayed development, anorexia, polydipsia (excessive thirst), polyphagia (excessive hunger), weight changes, cachexia (severe weight loss), hypothermia, dry mouth, clubbing of fingers, and other nonspecific symptoms. 26. Abnormal blood findings include elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, plasma viscosity abnormalities, red blood cell irregularities (anisocytosis, poikilocytosis), white blood cell abnormalities, hyperglycemia, abnormal serum enzyme levels, abnormal immunological findings, plasma protein abnormalities, and the presence of drugs or substances not normally found in blood. 27. Abnormal urine findings include proteinuria, glycosuria, chyluria, myoglobinuria, biliuria, hemoglobinuria, ketonuria, elevated drug levels, microbiological abnormalities, cytological abnormalities, and other unspecified findings. 28. Abnormal findings in other body fluids and tissues include cerebrospinal fluid, respiratory specimens, digestive specimens, and genital specimens. 29. Diagnostic imaging abnormalities include findings in the central nervous system, lungs, breast, skull, heart, liver, digestive tract, urinary organs, limbs, musculoskeletal system, and other body structures. 30. Abnormal function studies include results from the central nervous system, peripheral nervous system, pulmonary function, cardiovascular function, kidney function, liver function, thyroid function, endocrine function, and basal metabolic rate. 31. Ill-defined causes of mortality include sudden infant death syndrome, instantaneous death, death within 24 hours of symptom onset, unattended death, and other unspecified causes.
